author: andrew3019
body:
The single `orchestrator` role becomes two, the design document is rewritten for the new
model, and an adversarial review of the whole thing is folded in. Ten commits: six from the
work itself, four from the review.

## What changes

**A dispatcher and a lead, instead of one role at every scope.** A **dispatcher** is the top
of a tree and the only thing `sb start` creates. It holds no task and no context: it relays
what it was given to a child, adds nothing of its own about how the work should be
approached, and asks rather than guessing when the intent is unclear. Everything it is given
goes to a child, including a one-line question, so that the follow-up reaches the agent that
has the context. A **lead** owns one task end to end at any depth — it holds everything about
it, plans, splits, assigns disjoint files, synthesises and cleans up. That prompt is the old
orchestrator prompt, carried across essentially unchanged.

They were one role because the only difference looked like scope, and scope is told to an
agent at spawn. The split exists because "hold everything about your task" and "hold nothing"
do not fit in one prompt without a conditional, and a conditional gets read selectively.

**`orchestrator` still works, and resolves all the way to `lead`.** It is a config alias, so
a stale `--role orchestrator` gets a lead — not the fallback role, which cannot delegate at
all. The Role that comes back carries the new name, so the prompt, the board and the stored
row agree. Aliases are read from a repo's own settings as well as the shipped ones.

**Work that belongs in another repo stops the dispatcher.** It asks Andrew and starts nothing.
This is a stopping rule rather than a capability: there is no cross-repo spawn, and the one
real incident was an agent that, finding no way to root a child in another repo, forked a
worktree of *this* one and edited the other project through a path with nothing refusing it.

**`sb start` finds the running tops by the `is_top` stamp, not by the role name.** This was a
live defect the review caught: the lookup matched roots whose role equalled the configured top
role, and the rename made every existing row invisible — so the next bare `sb start` would
have opened a third top without the line telling Andrew how to get back to the one blocked and
waiting on him. Verified against a copy of the real store: empty before, both tops after.

**`DESIGN-TRUTH.md` is rewritten for the model** and corrected where it was not true of the
code, including what the dispatcher's home actually is and the fact that the dispatcher *role*
is not gated at all — a lead can ask for it, and only the prompt says not to.

## What is deliberately not in it

- **No tool-layer enforcement of what a dispatcher may do.** No gate, no blocked verbs. A
  dispatcher legitimately writes a handoff file, and a rule that cannot tell that from doing
  the work would either block the job or wave the work through. The prompt is the mechanism,
  which is why so much of this change is prompt text and why it is written to survive being
  read alongside rules that tell every other agent to do the work.
- **Real cross-repo dispatch is not built.** The store is per repo, so a child elsewhere would
  have no parentage, no messaging, no status, no board row and no cleanup reaching it — a
  multi-store fleet, not a flag. Whether it is ever built is open.
- **The herdr grouping limitation is accepted as it stands.** herdr can adopt a dispatcher as
  a repo's group parent if it is the first pane open in that repo's folder, which nests that
  repo's agents under it. Nothing breaks; the view muddles. The only real fix is in herdr and
  Andrew has chosen not to take it, so the document records it as a decided limitation rather
  than pending work.
- **`sb init` is still not refused to agents.** Only `sb start` is. The prompt says setting up
  another repo is Andrew's to do, and that sentence is a rule rather than a wall; whether to
  add the gate is unanswered.
- **Whether every level gets its own worktree is still open with Andrew.** Today only a
  dispatcher's children fork one and a lead's children share the lead's. The document was
  written to match the code, and several entries change if the answer is the other one.

## The review

Four rounds of adversarial review, each with a fresh reviewer and a different lens: the prompt
as a mechanism, the moment it lands on a running fleet, whether the trusted document is true
of the code, and the code read cold. Every round changed the artifact. What it produced, in
short: the flat "a dispatcher does none of the work" rule and the tie-break that makes it beat
the surrounding prompts, a verb for the moment a child finishes, the cleanup prohibition, the
stamp-based top lookup, the corrected document sentences, and the repo-layer fix for aliases.

Also here: `README` and the house-rules preset updated for the new names, and all twenty-four
line-range citations into `DESIGN-TRUTH.md` repaired, with a test that fails when one stops
pointing at an entry.

Suite green at **1206**, up from 1197.

body: Second follow-up to #40. My #45 fixed the template path but left the check rejecting **every legitimate single-platform image**. ## Problem `imagetools inspect --format '{{json .Image}}'` marshals an OCI image config, whose top-level key is **lowercase `config`** (capitalised `Env` nested inside). Confirmed against the real config blob for `ghcr.io/wyre-technology/autotask-mcp@sha256:b92a86a8…`: ``` top-level keys: architecture, config, created, history, os, rootfs has("Config")=false has("config")=true .config.Env = ["PATH=…","NODE_VERSION=26.7.0","NODE_ENV=production", …] ``` So `has("Config")` was false for every single-platform build, sending it down the platform-map branch, iterating the wrong values, and hard-failing. `docker image inspect` — a **different** command — *does* return capitalised `Config`. That is the trap. The check now accepts either. This blocked `autotask-mcp` **v2.32.5**'s deploy. I pulled the rejected digest from GHCR by hand: `application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json`, image config, 12 layers — a genuine image. body:
## Description

Enables the NVIDIA `secret-scan-trufflehog` pre-commit hook, pinned to `v0.3.0`,
as the first entry under `repos:` so scanning runs before any formatter rewrites
the working tree.

This adopts the centrally maintained hook published by `NVIDIA/security-workflows`
rather than a hand-rolled TruffleHog invocation, so the scanner version and its
per-platform checksums are bumped in one reviewed place instead of 27.

`v0.3.0` is pinned deliberately. It installs the scanner inside pre-commit's own
Python environment — removing the shell installer, so Windows works without Git
Bash — and it adds `--exclude-detectors=lob`. That exclusion matters here: a Lob
API key is `test_` followed by 35 characters, so the detector matches ordinary
pytest function names such as `test_gpu_conf_compute_attestation_report`, and
Lob's verifier reports them as *verified* — the one result class this hook fails
on.

Behaviour: scans only the files pre-commit supplies (staged files at commit time,
the push range at push time), reports verified secrets only, and fails closed on
a finding.

Deliberately **out of scope**:

- No `ci: skip:` block. That is prescribed for the hosted pre-commit.ci sandbox,
  which has no network access. No Triton repo uses pre-commit.ci — CI runs
  pre-commit from `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` — so it would be dead config.
- No `default_install_hook_types` change. Activation is a developer action;
  changing that key would alter install behaviour for *every* hook in the repo,
  not just this one. Tracked separately.

## Changes

- Add `NVIDIA/security-workflows` `secret-scan-trufflehog` @ `v0.3.0` as the
  first entry under `repos:`.

## Affected Files

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

## Test plan

- `pre-commit validate-config` — passes.
- `pre-commit run secret-scan-trufflehog --all-files` — passes, with **zero**
  pre-existing verified secrets, so CI does not break on merge.
- TruffleHog **3.95.9** confirmed installed into pre-commit's Python environment
  and executed, so the hook is functional rather than a silent no-op.
- Blast radius is bounded: `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` runs
  `pre-commit run --files` against PR-modified paths only, never `--all-files`.

## Caveats

Editing the config alone scans nothing. Each contributor must run once per clone:

```
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
```

Without the second, the `pre-push` stage stays dormant.

body:
Closes #65.

## Lots

Derived by replaying the trade ledger, never stored (ADR 0002). Each buy is a lot at its own date and price; a sell consumes them oldest-first. A Snapshot Holding — a provider position with no trades behind it — has no lots, which is reported as `snapshot`, not as one lot of unknown date.

Holding period is always computed: to the sell date when closed, to today while open. One year *or more* is long, so the anniversary itself counts. A 29 February lot turns long on 1 March, because a common year has no anniversary for it. A short-term lot shows how many days it still has to run.

## The gain, and the two conventions behind it

Splitting a Realised Gain needs *which* units left and *what* they cost. This takes the first from FIFO and leaves the second on the weighted average the app already books, so one sell keeps one Realised Gain — the tax split can't say 240 while the position says 250. `build_lots` consumes the ledger's own per-sell gains rather than re-deriving them, and asserts the two replays agree on sell order. Recorded as ADR 0003.

`realised_long + realised_short` always equals the ledger's Realised Gain, tested both on the Decimals and after rounding to cents — rounding each half on its own loses a cent whenever an odd number of them splits evenly (9.01 read as 4.50 + 4.50), which is exactly where the user would have seen it.

## Tax character

`GET /api/assets/{id}/tax-lots` reports `tax_character: false` and no lots for a wallet that is not Taxable — including a holding in no wallet at all. The gain there is never Reportable, so a long-versus-short answer would be noise dressed as advice. The derivation itself never sees a tax treatment, so the Wash Sale rule can still replay an IRA's ledger when it arrives. ADR 0002 now records that this is what "hidden" meant.

## UI

Expanding a position lists each wallet leg with its lots — acquisition date, quantity, unit price, cost, character, and days remaining for a short-term lot — plus that leg's long/short split of both the open position and what it has realised. The split is per wallet deliberately: tax character attaches to a wallet, so a consolidated cross-wallet split would blend a taxable leg with a Roth one into a figure no tax return could use.

## Tests

`backend/tests/test_tax_lots.py` — 28 tests, mostly pure: one year exactly, one day either side, both leap-year boundaries, open versus closed, FIFO matching, partial sales, a sale spanning two lots, re-bought positions, the cent-level invariant, and the tax-character gate for every treatment. Plus three API-level tests. Full suite: 2670 backend passed, 91 frontend passed; `tsc` and `eslint` clean.

## Known limits

A holding whose provider quantity predates its first manual trade reports lots for the traded slice only; the ledger becomes authoritative for it the moment a trade lands (ADR 0002), which is what restores agreement. Specific-identification is not offered — the lots derived here are what such a choice would pick from.

The well→stage formula that existed in **six independent copies** is now computed in exactly one module, and the monolithic calibration cache is split into geometry (catalog + sparse user overrides) and measured placement (deltas).

## The series

1. **Atomic cache writes, never fatal at import** — an interrupted write used to brick startup (`import control._def` raised on a truncated cache).
2. **Dead/stale state deleted** — zero-caller duplicate parser, write-only viewer field, dead ini keys in 8 templates, the 1536 selector's drifted hardcoded geometry.
3. **Dialog cancel restores the previous format** — two interlocking bugs; plus `select_format_silently()` kills the spurious index-0 emission that momentarily reconfigured the app for the wrong plate.
4. **One filename convention for custom plate images** (spaces preserved; legacy underscore accepted).
5. **Golden oracle** — exact-`==` pins on every producer site, offset-parameterized, with the sites' *disagreements* documented as tests.
6. **`PlateTransform` + `plate_transform_for`** — pure module; identity path `==`-identical to legacy arithmetic; `well_index_at` inverse; `nominal()` for display assets.

10. **`WellplateSettings` object replaces the 10-arg signal** — slots can no longer silently truncate the payload.
11. **Compute-time resolution in `ScanCoordinates`** — a calibration edit or offset change now applies to planning without a signal re-emit; the oracle's snapshot-vs-live disagreement test flips to agreement.
12. **Per-axis spacing/size + `well_shape` as derived data** — the 10-column CSV stays frozen; scalars broadcast; shape's name-based mapping becomes one code-side default.

16. **Navigation viewer maps stage↔pixel through the plate frame** — the background image is a *nominal* drawing, so forward (FOV boxes) applies R(−θ) about A1 and inverse (double-click) applies R(+θ); planned FOVs land on the wells they will image and clicks navigate to where wells actually sit. Unrotated path kept bit-for-bit legacy (asserted); rotation resolved at call time, once per batch redraw. 5 tests incl. pixel→mm→pixel round trip.
17. **Out-of-travel FOVs dropped loudly** — every region producer counts travel drops into `ScanCoordinates.out_of_travel` (queryable by the upcoming wizard) and warns with exact counts, instead of quietly imaging fewer FOVs than selected. Lifecycle-correct (re-add/remove/clear purge). 8 tests.
18. **Provenance stamps on saved coordinate CSVs** — one JSON comment line records format, effective A1, rotation + source, and save time; "Load Coordinates" warns (but still loads) when the placement has since changed, naming exactly what moved. Legacy unstamped files load as before. 8 tests.

Implements IMPROVEMENTS.md §1.6: `check_untyped_defs` is now on globally, with a mechanically generated per-module baseline that can only shrink.

## Today's numbers

Reproduced with the exact toolchain CI uses (`mypy==1.16.1` from the pre-commit pin, with numpy): enabling `check_untyped_defs` on current `main` surfaces **2,166 errors in 185 files** (IMPROVEMENTS.md measured 2,172 in 186 at the time of writing; the tree has moved since). The worst offenders are unchanged: `Bio/Align/bigbed.py` (148), `Bio/Seq.py` (120), `Bio/Blast/_parser.py` (118), `Bio/Restriction/Restriction.py` (89), `Bio/GenBank/Scanner.py` (55).

## Scoreboard

**179 modules baselined** (185 failing on the original tree, minus 5 fixed here and `Bio.Pathway` fixed in #97). The number in `.mypy.ini` only goes down.

## The ratchet rule

Stated in the `.mypy.ini` header: baseline entries may only be **removed** (after fixing the module so it passes with `check_untyped_defs` on), never added. New modules are born checked.

## Why per-module `check_untyped_defs = False`, not `ignore_errors = True`

IMPROVEMENTS.md proposed `ignore_errors = True` per module, but that is a much blunter ratchet: it silences *everything* in the module, including the errors mypy already catches today without `check_untyped_defs` — so a baselined module could quietly regress on checks that used to protect it. Per-module `check_untyped_defs = False` preserves the status quo *exactly*: every check that ran yesterday still runs on every module, and clean/new modules additionally get their function bodies checked. Verified: with the baseline in place, the pinned mypy run on the full tree is green.

The sections were generated by script from mypy's own error output (error file list → module names), not hand-typed.

## Proof the ratchet catches regressions

Added this deliberately broken untyped function to `Bio/File.py` (a clean, non-baselined module), ran the pinned mypy, then reverted it:

```python
def _ratchet_demo():
    handle = open("x")
    return handle.made_up_attribute
```

New config catches it:

```
Bio/File.py:637:12: error: "TextIOWrapper[_WrappedBuffer]" has no attribute
"made_up_attribute"  [attr-defined]
        return handle.made_up_attribute
               ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 304 source files)
```

The same injected error under the old behaviour (`--no-check-untyped-defs`) passes clean: `Success: no issues found in 304 source files`. That is exactly the class of latent `AttributeError` §1.6 is about.

## Five trivial fixes (second commit)

Five modules each had exactly **one** error, all `[var-annotated]` — an empty container literal mypy cannot infer. Annotating the literal is a runtime no-op, so these come off the baseline instead of onto it:

| Module | Annotation | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| `Bio/SeqIO/FastaIO.py` | `lines: list[str] = []` | only ever holds `line.rstrip()` strings, joined with `"".join` |
| `Bio/AlignIO/MauveIO.py` | `seqs: dict[str, str] = {}` | keys are regex-group id strings, values built by `+=` of line strings |
| `Bio/ExPASy/ScanProsite.py` | `match: dict[str, str \| int] = {}` | values are `int(self.content)` or `self.content` (str), keyed by element name |
| `Bio/Pathway/Rep/Graph.py` | `self._adjacency_list: dict = {}` | keys are caller-supplied node objects of no constrained type; `sorted()` over the keys rules out `object`, so bare `dict` |
| `Bio/Graphics/DisplayRepresentation.py` | `self._label_info: dict = {}` | keys are caller-supplied segment names, values unconstrained labels |

Everything non-obvious stays baselined. `Bio.Pathway` was deliberately left for the separate bug fix in #97 rather than papered over with an annotation. With #97 now merged, a third commit removes `[mypy-Bio.Pathway]` from the baseline. The separate `[mypy-Bio.Pathway.Rep.MultiGraph]` entry remains.

## What I verified

- `uvx --with numpy mypy==1.16.1` (the CI pin) on the tree: **green**, 304 source files — both at the baseline commit and at HEAD.
- `uvx pre-commit run mypy --all-files`: **Passed**.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.
- Rebuilt the C extensions in place, then the full offline suite (`Tests/run_tests.py --offline`, CPython 3.12): **522 tests, 0 failures, 25 skipped** (missing optional dependencies), exit 0.
- Not tested: PyPy, and mypy versions other than the pinned 1.16.1.

## Problema

Nada validava o código antes do merge. Um pull request podia quebrar o build e isso só aparecia quando o Render falhava no deploy, que é o lugar mais caro e mais tarde possível para descobrir.

Já aconteceu: o deploy quebrou com `Cannot find module '/opt/render/project/src/dist/main'` porque o `prisma/seed.ts` passou a entrar no build e mudou a estrutura da pasta `dist`. Um passo de build rodando no pull request teria mostrado a falha antes de qualquer coisa chegar em produção.

## O que este PR faz

Adiciona um workflow do GitHub Actions que roda em todo pull request para a `main` e em todo push nela, executando lint e build.

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**
- Instala dependências com `npm ci`, que respeita o lockfile e garante que a validação use exatamente as mesmas versões do ambiente local.
- Roda `prisma generate` antes de lint e build, porque o Prisma Client é gerado e não versionado. Numa máquina limpa ele não existe, e sem esse passo tudo quebraria por um motivo que não é o código.
- Usa uma `DATABASE_URL` fictícia. O `prisma generate` apenas lê o schema e não abre conexão, mas o schema referencia a variável.

**`.nvmrc`**
- Fixa a versão do Node. O arquivo é lido tanto pelo GitHub Actions quanto pelo Render, então um único lugar passa a controlar a versão nos dois ambientes. Sem isso, o CI poderia validar numa versão diferente da que roda em produção.

**`lint:ci` no `package.json`**
- O script `lint` existente usa `--fix`, o que é correto no desenvolvimento e problemático no CI. O runner é descartável, então a correção seria descartada, e uma violação corrigível automaticamente deixaria o CI verde enquanto o código versionado continuaria com o problema. O novo script apenas reporta.

body:
## Description

Enables the NVIDIA `secret-scan-trufflehog` pre-commit hook, pinned to `v0.3.0`,
as the first entry under `repos:` so scanning runs before any formatter rewrites
the working tree.

This adopts the centrally maintained hook published by `NVIDIA/security-workflows`
rather than a hand-rolled TruffleHog invocation, so the scanner version and its
per-platform checksums are bumped in one reviewed place instead of 27.

`v0.3.0` is pinned deliberately. It installs the scanner inside pre-commit's own
Python environment — removing the shell installer, so Windows works without Git
Bash — and it adds `--exclude-detectors=lob`. That exclusion matters here: a Lob
API key is `test_` followed by 35 characters, so the detector matches ordinary
pytest function names such as `test_gpu_conf_compute_attestation_report`, and
Lob's verifier reports them as *verified* — the one result class this hook fails
on.

Behaviour: scans only the files pre-commit supplies (staged files at commit time,
the push range at push time), reports verified secrets only, and fails closed on
a finding.

Deliberately **out of scope**:

- No `ci: skip:` block. That is prescribed for the hosted pre-commit.ci sandbox,
  which has no network access. No Triton repo uses pre-commit.ci — CI runs
  pre-commit from `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` — so it would be dead config.
- No `default_install_hook_types` change. Activation is a developer action;
  changing that key would alter install behaviour for *every* hook in the repo,
  not just this one. Tracked separately.

## Changes

- Add `NVIDIA/security-workflows` `secret-scan-trufflehog` @ `v0.3.0` as the
  first entry under `repos:`.

## Affected Files

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

## Test plan

- `pre-commit validate-config` — passes.
- `pre-commit run secret-scan-trufflehog --all-files` — passes, with **zero**
  pre-existing verified secrets, so CI does not break on merge.
- TruffleHog **3.95.9** confirmed installed into pre-commit's Python environment
  and executed, so the hook is functional rather than a silent no-op.
- Blast radius is bounded: `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` runs
  `pre-commit run --files` against PR-modified paths only, never `--all-files`.

## Caveats

Editing the config alone scans nothing. Each contributor must run once per clone:

```
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
```

Without the second, the `pre-push` stage stays dormant.

Tracks #238 — close only after published-artifact qualification.

## What changed

- Adds repository profile schema v3 under `@vespeneventures/governance/repository` with caller-owned `rootEntries`.
- Adds pure `validateRepositoryRootEvaluationInput` and `evaluateRepositoryRoot` APIs. Unknown direct children, missing required entries, and observed prohibited entries fail closed.
- Requires every declared direct child to carry an explicit `canonical`, `extension`, `exception`, `compatibility-alias`, or `legacy-artifact` classification and a separate `required`, `allowed`, or `prohibited` disposition.
- Keeps repository-root vocabulary in the existing repository subpath. Account-container discovery and composition remain caller-owned, so no broad governance workspace package or subpath is introduced.
- Updates conventions machine guidance from one workspace authority to discovery and composition across multiple account-owned workspace planes.
- Leaves provisioning implementation unchanged.

## Public API

New functions:

- `validateRepositoryRootEvaluationInput(value)`
- `evaluateRepositoryRoot(value)`

New constants and types:

- `PREVIOUS_REPOSITORY_PROFILE_VERSION`
- `RepositoryProfileV3`
- `RepositoryRootEntry`
- `RepositoryRootEntryClassification`
- `RepositoryRootEntryDisposition`
- `RepositoryRootEvaluationInput`
- `RepositoryRootEntryEvaluation`
- `RepositoryRootEvaluation`
- `RepositoryRootEvaluationStatus`
- `RepositoryRootFinding`
- `RepositoryRootFindingRule`

`REPOSITORY_PROFILE_VERSION` advances to `3`. Closed v1 and v2 profiles remain explicitly supported.

## Consumer migration

1. Upgrade direct consumers to `@vespeneventures/governance@~0.10.0`.
2. Existing v1 and v2 profiles remain valid without edits.
3. To prove an exact root, adopt schema v3 and declare every admitted direct child in `rootEntries`.
4. Discover direct children outside Foundry and pass only normalized names as `observedEntries`.
5. Treat `invalid` and `nonconforming` reports as fail-closed; the caller retains ownership of inventory, observations, paths, retention, precedence, and any mutation.

The deprecated `@vespeneventures/repository@0.4.0` compatibility package forwards the new API. Other governance compatibility packages receive patch releases only to keep their 0.x dependency ranges linked.

## Proposed package versions

- `@vespeneventures/governance@0.10.0`
